text:
Kirill Kaprizov leads the NHL with 16 goals, and the more impressive number attached to him is 12.3. That's the expected goals his shots have been worth in 18 games: he's getting to dangerous ice constantly. Strip out the hot finishing and he'd still have a dozen.

The finishing is hot, though. He's shooting 29% after 17% last season, and our numbers expect that to come down. Friday's four-point night against San Jose stretched his point streak to seven games, and his line with Matt Boldy and Joel Eriksson Ek is pushing play hard. Quinn Hughes put it plainly after that game: "I just feel like we can tilt the ice when they're out there" (via Heather Rule of NHL.com). With Kaprizov on the ice, the Wild take 62% of the five-on-five expected goals.

Our projection has him at 52 goals, with a range from 43 to 62. A fifth-round pick, 135th overall in 2015, chasing the goal-scoring lead in November is a good story whether or not the shooting holds. Watch the shot count: 56 in 18 games is where the lasting goals come from.
headline: The league's top goal scorer, explained
